andrew: Heads up — reproducible memory growth when continuous batching is enabled on long-context runs. Staging load with ~2k token sequences; kv-cache keeps growing instead of stabilizing, eviction spikes and we get occasional H-O-L blocking during batch merges.

sam: which model / config? any flamegraphs or heap profiles?

andrew: repro steps: spin up cont-batching enabled + merge_threshold=3, run long-chat workload for ~30 minutes. I captured a heap diff and a perf flame for the runtime thread. Flame shows a long path through `batch_merge -> acquire_kv_lock -> reclaim_slab -> alloc_slot` repeated.

andrew: quick command I used:
```
./tools/run_stress.sh --model q4-prod --cont-batch=true --merge-thresh=3 --seq=2048 --qps=20 > /tmp/stress.log 2>&1
```
flame link: https://perf.internal/flames/1748765432 (redacted)

perf-bot: automated trace summary: 14% of runtime CPU in `reclaim_slab`, 9% in `alloc_slot`, tail latency 99.9th increased from 120ms -> 340ms after ~12m, kv-eviction-rate 0.7/s -> 4.8/s.

maria: sounds like fragmentation + churn. If merges create batches that interleave very different seq lengths, KV slot reuse drops and we allocate new slabs instead of reusing fragments. That fits the repeated reclaim->alloc pattern. Have you checked kv_fragmentation_ratio and avg_live_slots?

andrew: captured some counters (snippet):
```
kv_live_slots: 1872 -> 3920
kv_frag_ratio: 0.14 -> 0.62
merged_batch_size_avg: 4.1
headwait_ms_avg: 23 -> 190
```
So frag_ratio climbs as the run continues. Turning off merge lowered frag_ratio to ~0.18 in the same test window.

jacob: interesting — could also be kernel selection interaction. When merges produce larger effective batch lengths, runtime may switch to the 'wide-kernel' that keeps more meta state per request, increasing memory pressure and changing allocation patterns. Do we have kernel-selection logs?

andrew: yes, kernel logs show switch to kernel_v2_wide at ~10m mark when merged_batch_size_avg > 3. That correlates exactly with the moment reclaim hotpath spikes.

sam: quick mitigation: avoid merging across large seq_len variance. We should add a heuristic: only merge if stddev(seq_len) < X or estimated_kv_reuse > Y. Cheap estimation can use prefix-match ratio.

maria: agree. Also consider a fast-path reuse bucket for small KV fragments so we can avoid slab reclaim thrash when merges are frequent. We could bias allocator to reuse > 75% from LRU bins before new slab alloc.

jacob: another low-risk experiment: gate kernel switch on merged_batch_cumulative_tokens threshold instead of batch_size alone. If kernel_v2_wide triggers only when tokens per batch > T, we might avoid the memory regression.

andrew: ran quick toggles: disabling merge removes memory growth but increases p99 latency ~30ms. Gate-on-tokens prevented kernel switch and kept memory stable in 20m run, latency hit ~+10ms p99.

sam: sounds promising. We should record these knobs in a short AB test: (A) merge on, kernel switch allowed (current) (B) merge on but token-gate for kernel switch (C) merge off. Measure kv_frag_ratio, headwait_ms, p50/p99, and cost.

maria: for telemetry add: `kv_frag_ratio`, `kv_reuse_rate`, `merged_batch_seq_stddev`, `merged_batch_tokens`, `headwait_ms`, `kernel_selected`, `slab_reclaims`. That will let us automate rollback if frag ratio exceeds threshold.

andrew: created a PR with the token-gate patch and extra counters (WIP). I'll run an overnight soak on staging with the test matrix. Assigning follow-ups: andrew -> run soak + upload flames, sam -> add merge heuristic prototype, maria -> allocator reuse tweak proposal, jacob -> kernel gate experiment.

jacob: also logging a short term action: add an alert on sustained kv_frag_ratio > 0.5 for 10m during cont-batching to catch regressions early.

andrew: Perfect. I'll post results tomorrow AM. Thanks all :thumbsup:
